newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Dec 12.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Predicting that inflation will stay low for at least the next year and a half, the Reserve Bank of Australia yesterday cut official interest rates by a further half a percent, surprising financial markets and triggering immediate flow-on cuts for busines, credit card and home loan borrowers. Page 1.

The Federal Government yesterday released its petroleum reform blueprint, which would see petrol prices deregulated and oil terminal access opened up to independent operators. The blueprint hopes to increase competition, but has received a mixed reaction from within the industry. Page 1.

The Minerals Council of Australia said yesterday in its minerals industry survey that land access problems such as native title claims and expanding forest reserves had pushed Australian minerals companies to invest 41 percent of their 1995/96 exploration budget overseas. Page 3.

The Federal Department of Transport yesterday revealed that Qantas Airways Ltd was increasing pressure on its head-to-head rival Ansett Australia, with the airline lifting its slice of passengers flying into and out of Australia 40.3 percent in August, the highest since November 1995. Page 3.

Newly appointed Coles Myer chief executive Dennis Eck believes the retailing giant already has to form the right strategies to restore its credibility within the financial community and among consumers. Eck will not be making any real changes for Coles Myer, as his immediate concern is to sustain growth in Coles Supermarkets, rebuild the K-Mart brand, improve the image of Myer Grace and repatriate the loss-making World 4 Kids chain. Page 17.

The Nielsen ScanTrak retail industry survey for RetailWorld, the supermarket industry's publication has found Coles Supermarkets was Australia's fastest growing grocery chain for the past year, yet it still needs to catch up to Woolworths Ltd, which increased its national share of the A$19 billion per year dry grocery market by 1.2 percent to 34.3 percent. Page 17.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Financial markets were rattled yesterday by the Reserve Bank's surprise 0.5 percent cut in official interest rates, with the Australian dollar falling more than one U.S. cent from its previous close, bond markets rallying strongly - cutting yields on 90-day bank bills by 55 basis points to 5.90 percent and on 10-year bonds from 7.35 percent to 7.19 percent. Economists were quick to warn the cut could overheat the economy and result in increased rates next year. Page 23.

The Council of Financial Supervisors - consisting of the Reserve Bank, the Australian Securities Commission, the Insurance and Superannuation Commission and the Australian Financial Institutions Commission - yesterday rejected proposals for creation of a sole financial regulator, warning this could see consumers misled about their level of protection. Page 23.

The general consensus in Australia's corporate world on yesterday's surprise interest rate cut was that it was too little, too late. Harvey Norman managing director Gerry Harvey was joined by the Australian Chamber of Manufacturers and the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry in saying the RBA should have acted more decisively when it cut rates by one percent in July and half a percent in November. Page 23.

BHP Petroleum chief executive John O'Connor said yesterday the division will adopt a "liquidation scenario" unless its current A$350 million exploration programme adds substantially to its resource base. While O'Connor said he was optimistic about the opportunities for growth, he remained realistic about the strategies to use should his aggressive investment programme fail. Page 23.

Anaconda Nickel NL yesterday finalised the sale of 40 percent of the A$900 million Murrin Murrin nickel deposit in Western Australia to Swiss commodities house Glencore International AG. Anaconda executive director George Macdonald indicated the finalistion of the agreement should see the deposit edging closer to production. Page 24.

At yesterday's Canberra launch of the Minerals Council of Australia's annual minerals industry survey, which found that 41 percent of investment by major Australian companies went into offshore projects in 1995/96, BHP chairman-elect Jerry Ellis warned that Australia's low sovereign risk profile would erode if the government does not have a positive approach to mineral developments. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Financial markets were surprised yesterday by the Reserve Bank's third cut in official interest rates in six months, promoting a mad scramble that drove the Australian dollar down a cent and saw market rates tumble. Business groups and executives welcomed the cut but many criticised the timing. Page 25.

Retail executives were cautiously optimistic about the benefits from yesterday's interest rate cut, saying it has come too late to have an impact on this year's Christmas sales. Most retailers believe the flow-through from the cut will be felt next year as consumers await the post-Christmas sales. Page 25.

In the first major reform to the petroleum industry in 16 years, the federal government announced the deregulation of price setting, open access to oil terminals, increased monitoring of prices, and the establishment of a code for fair business practice. The changes should see country petrol prices drop. Page 25.

Australis Media's new chief executive officer Sean O'Halloran said yesterday Australis may survive as a single entity and there was no need to merge with other pay-TV operators Foxtel or Optus Vision. O'Halloran said after the company's annual general meeting that there were a number of options for the company to grow its own business. Page 27.

With the collapse of Digicall, Vodafone's largest reseller, the U.K.-owned company has seen its share of the digital mobile telephone market eroded in recent weeks, with Telstra becoming the big winner, securing about 48 percent of the market, which has inreased to about 1.2 million. Page 27.

Seven Network executive chairman Kerry Stokes will fly to Los Angeles tomorrow to meet with Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer's new owner, Kirk Kerkorian, and managing director Frank Mancusco to concentrate on the film studio's controversial accounts. The meeting is epected to be heated, but Stokes played down any potential conflict yesterday. Page 27.
THE AGE

Following the third official cut in interest rates since July yesterday, financial markets were already preparing for a possible further easing in monetary policy in the new year, after being surprised by yesterday's announcement. Page B1.

Representatives from large retailers Woolworths and Coles Myer and the Retail Traders' Association said the latest cut in interest rates has come too late to improve Christmas sales, yet they remain optimistic as spending is up 12 percent on last year and credit card rate cuts are expected to fall in the new year. Page B1.

The world trade ministers meeting in Singapore is looking at a draft agreement that could see tariffs on information technology and telecommunications products abolished. Australian officials yesterday said they were satisfied with the agreement, however negotiations are continuing over which products the agreement would include. Page B1.

Although 1996 would still be General Motors Holden's eighth consecutive year in profit, managing director Bill Hamel said yesterday the car maker's profitability would be down by 10 to 20 percent. Hamel also confirmed Holden was developing left-hand drive Commodores for Middle Eastern markets and could soon become the sole GM world source for a rear-wheel drive platform. Page B2.

Since the High Court's Mabo judgement was handed down in mid-1992, offshore exploration as a proportion of total mining exploration spending had increased from 27.3 percent to 40.5 percent, according to Minerals Council of Australia president Jerry Ellis. Ellis, who is also BHP's chairman elect, said the uncertainty generated by native title claims was pushing Australian miners overseas. Page B3.

Listed chemicals group Incitec is conducting a feasibility study into building a A$500 million fertiliser plant in Victoria and expects to know the result by mid-1997. Incitec managing director Jim Babon yesterday ruled out a project in Queensland and said that if the plant proceeds in Victoria, 400,000 tonnes of urea and 100,000 tonnes of ammonia will be produced. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
